FOREWORD

0.1 Tins Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Instrtution on 31 December 1981, after the draft finahzcd by the Subsurface Exploration Sectional Committee had been approved by the CIvIl Engineering DIvision Council. 0.2 With the increasing demand for power in the country, an increasingly ~ large number of power houses (hydroelectrIc, thermal, and nuclear) are being built, One of the major reqmrements In planning, design and construction of these power houses is proper and adequate subsurface Investigation. The object of subsurface and related site Investigation IS to provide the engineer with as much mforrnation as possible about the existing conditions, for example, the thickness of overburden and other geological features of the area. This code has been prepared to serve a" a guide in such mvestigations.

0.2.1 The methods of subsurface investigation enable vertical sections
of the strata to be drawn based on tn-stiu tests, samples tested for determining characteristics such as shear strength parameters, bearing capacity of the SOlI, permeabihty, water table, and sorl or rock type classification. This

information together with the normal topographical survey provides the engineer with complete details of the site and enables hnn to prepare
economical designs for the power house structures.

0.3 In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to co-ordination among the standards and pracnccs prevailing III different ccuntrres in addition to relating it to the practices In the field In this country. 0.4 For the purpose of decidmg whether a particular requirement of this standard IS complied WIth, the final value, observed or calculated, expressmg the result of a test, shall be rounded off In accordance with IS .2-1960*. The number of significant places retained In the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value In this standard.
�Rules for rounding off numerical values ( reused )

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard gives gwdance on the type, extent and details of subsurface exploration needed in connection with power houses of the following types:
a) Hydroelectric power houses :

I) Surface power houses, and ii) Underground power houses;
b) Thermal power houses, and c) Nuclear power houses.

1.1.1 This standard provides guidehnes for planning the exploratory work, through various stages of the project development. These recommendations may have to be modified for mdividual projects, depending upon the site condinons and other condrnons pecuhar to each project, such as height and importance of the power home and the heterogenesty of foundation for1D3tions.
1.2 The term subsurface exploration, as used herem, covers all types of exploration connected with determination of the nature and extent of soil at or near the power house SIte. 1.3 This code does not, however, cover the types and methods of exploration for materials of construction for power houses such as SOli and rock and material for riprap.

2. GENERAL
2.1 In the design of some components of power house structure foundations, special attention is given to the effect of Vibrations and sensitivity to settlements. Hence, the results of subsurface exploration should provide enough data for the study of these features and exploration should be very detailed and thorough Faults, shear zones, weathered horizon and joints found in the rock mass constituting the foundation shall be demarcated. All changes in rock type and formation contacts shall be studied 10 detail. 2.2 The type and extent of exploration shall be commensurate With the size and importance of the project and Will depend upon the size of the power house and the type of foundation.
2.3 Subsurface explorations in connection with a power house shall cover a specified area around the power house site and shall be carried out to a

4

IS , 10060 - 1981
specified depth. Depending upon the type of power house, investigation shall be required for the following areas of the power house complex: a) Forebay, b) Penstocks, c) Locations of turbine and generators,

d) Afterbay,
e) Switch and transformer yards, f) Foundations of high stacks ( chimneys ), g) Area of boilers,
h) Nuclear reactors and ancillaries, and

j) Other power house components.

2.3.1 A complete programme of exploration shall be able to give information regarding the following points :
a) Types of different soil and rock masses that exit in the foundation and abutments; b) The location, sequence, thickness and aerial extent of eaclwsoil/rock stratum, including a descripnon and classification of the soils, their mineral and chemical constituents and their structure, stratification in the undisturbed state, sigruficant geological or other structural features, such as buried channels,
seams, JOInts and fissures,

c) The depth and type of bedrock as well as the location, sequence, thickness, areal extent, altitude, depth of weathering, soundness, and description of rock in each rock stratum within the depth of exploration; d) The charactenstics of the ground water, including whether the
water table IS perched or normal, Influent or affluent, direction

of flow of ground wa ter , depth of and pressure in artesian zones and chemical quahty of ground water; and e) Engineering properties of the overburden and rocks.

2.3.2 Exploration shall also be needed for study of the followmg problems:
a) Determination of stability of slope adjacent to plant excavanon; b) Determination of the stability and erosion characteristics of the tall race channel ( to know if hning IS required ) , c) In the case of thermal stations, if water IS to be obtained from wells, subsurface studies directed to location of wells and their design, and the effects of suction and depletion of subsoil water level in the power house structure foundations (see Note);

5

IS : 10060 - 1981
NOTE - Possibility of sulphuric acid and sulphates formed by the percolation of water through ash dumps of thermal plants using coal reaching the foundations and their Impact. such as attack on concrete/steel or Ieachmg of certain salts causmg foundation settlement may also be cxammed

d) In hydroelectric power houses the effect of seepage water on subsurface materral ; e) Landslides, Rockfalls and Avalanches - The stability of glacial and fluroglacial matenal with thm soil cap, creep of soil covered hill slopes, etc, shall be studied In the case of power houses placed at the foot of a hill or on a steep hillside, the hill slope shall be exarnmed for existing or potential landslides or rockfalls. The location of power houses in high altitude areas shall take into account the possibility of avalanches affecting the stability of the power houses; and f) In the case of nuclear power houses located on seashore, shoreline stability may be assessed. 1.4 For SOlis, test in accordance with IS: 2131-1963* and 4.3, 4.4 and 12.2 of IS 6955-1973t may be conducted at the required locations.

2.4.1 Wherever drillmg in rock is resorted to, NX or larger size would be preferably used as large diameter cores would be useful for studying jomt patterns and fracturing (see IS : 6926-1973~ ). As loads are heavy, shear tests on rock samples may be necessary.
2.5 For general prmciples and procedures to be followed for mvesuganon and samplmg, reference may be made to IS . 1892-1979�. For exploration by pits, trenches, bormg, dnfts and shafts, references may be made to 7 to n of IS : 6955-1973t. 2.6 The extent of foundation exploration required for power houses of given size vanes from sire to site, depending on the subsurface conditions, and cannot be adequately Visualized m advance The exploration generally proceeds in stages, the details of each stage growmg out of the one before It normally {ollows a learn-as-you-go procedure In which characrerrsncs of the subsurface SOlIs and condinons are developed In progressively greater detail as the exploration proceeds.

2.7 The subsurface exploration required for a power house are grouped under the following stages:
a) b) c) d) Reconnaissance stage investigatrons ; Preliminary stage mvesriganons ; Detailed or pre-design stage mvestigations ; and Construction stage mvestigation

2.7.1 The type of invesngarions required for the last 3 stages wJ!1 be the same; only difference being m the details of mformation gathered, quanta. tively. Therefore, after describing the reconnaissance stage investigations, the type of information required for the last 3 stages are described together and then the quantitative detail of information for all the 3 stages. If it is found that the properties of foundation material vary too much, then, in each bay, information shall be gathered at least at 3 points.

2.8 Type of Infonnation Required
2.8.1 Settlement

2.8.1.1 For finding out the safety of the power house, m so far as . uruforrn and equal settlement are concerned, the following investigations shall be carried out:
a) A chart showmg the strata below final foundation level up to one-and-a-half times the width of the substructure of the power house housing the main generating equipment shall be prepared. Investiganons shall be earned out to find out If there are compressible day or other objectionable layers witlun this depth. In rock WIth adequate bearing characteristirs the bore holes need to penetrate only about 8 m. For the purpose of Investig-ation, unless otherwise known, It may be assumed that the foundation of hydroelectric plants generally are 9 to 12 m below the ongina! ground surface. b) The safe beanng pressure at the foundation level of the power stanon shall be found out m (I) dry, (ii) normal, and (ui) submerged sod condrtrons

2.8.1.2 In order to predict any settlement, modulus of the foundanon soil, that I~, intensity of SOIl pressure divided by the settlement shall be found for all different materials met wrth in the substrata up to depths indicated in 2.8.1.1. This modulus shall be found for dry, normal and submerged conditions of the strata 2.8.2 Slzdmg - For the stability of the power house 1t IS Important to see that the horizontal forces aellnR above any plane and tending to slide the structure along that plane are not greater than the resisung forces of Fricuon or the shear strength of the materials of foundations forming the plane.

2.8.3 Ground Water Cond.tzons - In order to find the extent of submergence of the soil, !ugh and low spring levels at the site of the power house shall be recorded 2.8.4 Dynamu Stabtltry - For the determination of dynamic stabtltty, dynamic properties of the soil shall be determined in accordance with IS : 5249-1977* and also to the requirements of IS : 1893-1975t. 2.8.5 Any other characteristics required by the field or design engineer for a particular localtty shall also be determined.

3. HYDROELECTRIC SURFACE POWER HOUSES
3.1 Reconnaissance Stage Investigations 3.1.1 The scope of investigation during this stage IS confined to the investigation of the suitabihty of constructing a surface hydel power house m the area where the required drop IS available to create head for generation of electncity The mvesngation with the general reconnaissance of the area shall he done on I . 50 000 scale topo-maps havmg contour interval ...c. 20 m, so as to estabhsh broad topographical and geological features df the foundation material. 3.1.2 In case the site is near hilly slopes, stabihty of the hill slopes shall be mvesngated. In sites subject to avalanches, the direction of avalanche routes and the magnitude of avalanches shall be studied.

3.1.3 In case of SItes at high altitude, investigation shall clearly bear out the suitabihty of foundation materral with partIcular reference to the following conditions:
a) Permafrost, and b) Stabrhty of glacial and diluroglacial material with a thin cap.
SOlI

3.1.4 The presence and extent of artesian pressures below the foundation material shall be investigated to deterrnme whether the site is suitable for power house location or not.
3.2 Preliminary Stage Investigations

3.2.1 Objectwes and Types and Method, of Exploratton - Durmg this stage data for formulation of the project are collected. The coverage of exploration

shall be adequate for examination of the feasibihty which includes estimation of the cost and evaluation of the benefits. This stage also includes studies for preliminary choice of the alignment as well as the height of the power house. This stage of exploration includes the following. a) Exploration by test pits, trenches, drifts and shafts; b) Exploration by geophvsrcal methods, c) Exploration by drilling using coring and non- coring methods or by other bormg methods, d) Deterrmnation of the depth water table and evaluation of field permeability; observation of temperature, pressure and discharge of springs not at the surface or in exploratory borings,
trenches, etc;

e) Field penetration and field density test in overburden; and f) Laboratory tests on representative samples and undisturbed samples for the determination of engineering properties of the overburden material. 3.2.2 In order to fix the preliminary drmensions of the power station and its general lay-out it will be necessary to give the information required in 3.4 3.2.3 After locatmg the most suitable site from the results of reconnaissance stage investigation, information specified in 2.8 shall be found out for one point only situated at the middle of possible power house layout. 3.2.4 In case of location in alluvium soil, investigation shall bring out presence, if any, of layers of silt, peat, quick sand or a high content of clay which might cause foundation problems. 3.3 Detailed (Pre-construction) Investigation Stage 3.3.1 These invesngauons are required for obtaimng data required for detailed design of all structures related to the power house. These investigauons shall be conducted at the final location of the power house and appurtenant works fixed from preliminary stage investigations. 3.3.2 In this stage of mvestigation, all data required for detailed design and preparation of construction drawings shall be collected. Close coordination IS essential between the work of the organizations for exploration, geological work and design.
9

IS : 10060 - 1981 3.3.3 Investigations at this stage shall cornprrse the following:
a) Intensive exploration by additional drilling and pittmg ( trenches and shafts where found necessary) of the foundation to
deterrmne spatial distribution and characteristics of different

types of foundation materials in relation to specific design features; b) Use of geophysical methods to define in greater detail the subsurface conditions, such as the depth to bed rock or depth to water table in specific sections of the power house base. During this stage, use of borehole geophysical methods, such as electric logging, as and when reqmred, may be found
advantageous to define particular characterrstics of overburden

and bed rock, c) Defining of geohydrological characterrsncs of the foundations and their environments through pumping in or pumping out tests as dictated by site conditions ; d) Ascertaining the groutability of foundations through trial grouting of specified reaches; and e) Special field tests hke blasting tests (to determine whether the material IS liable to liquefy under seismic disturbance) and field shear tests wherever found necessary

3.3.4 Information specified in 3.4 may be obtained for at least one point SItuated at the middle of the unit bay, erection bay and control bay. More boreholes may be required, depending upon the geological conditions. 3.4 Construction Stage - Construction stage exploration shall arm at making available data generally for the evaluation of specific foundation
preparation and treatment. In case, after actual excavation, it is found that the properties of foundation material vary tao much, then, In each

bay, mformauon shall be gathered at least at 3 points. A complete record of the foundation features shall be maintamed at this stage. This IS essential for the solut Ion of post construcnon problems, if any.

4. HYDROELECTRIC UNDERGROUND POWER HOUSES 4.1 Reconnaissance Stage Investigations 4.1.1 The scope of invesugauons durmg this stage IS confined to the
selection of the most SUitable sites from the geological considerations,

besides satisfying the engmeerIng requirements The investigation shall

10

IS : l00Ci0 - 1981
proceed with the general reconnaissance of the area on I : 50 000 scale topo-maps having contour of 20 m to establish broad geomorophological features. Lithological characters and altitude of the host rock and its major jointing, shear zone and pattern, and the major structural and tectonic features, such as folds, faults and thrusts, shall be recorded and their significance in terms of the seisrmcitv of the area shall be evaluated After eliminating obviously unsatisfactory sites, reconnaissance stage explorations shall be done to establish the nature and extent of overburden cover and major active or potential slide features along the slope. Preferably, thinly bedded fissile and hrghly fractured rocks shall be avoided and slope configuration shall be studied WIth reference to stabihty and availability of sound rock cover over the cavitv A programme of surface and subsurface mvesngations shall be chalked out for the selected site to establish the depth of open and slump JOints or potential slide mass as well as depth to sound rock over the proposed cavity. The reconnaissance stage investigations shall Include those mdicated in 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4.

4.1.2 Surveys 4.1.2.1 Topographic survev on I : I 000 scale shall be carried out, extending from the head race tunnel end to the tail race tunnel end and covering the hill slope for 150 m on either SIde of the proposed SItes of the power house structure and penstocks. This shall be used as a base map for detailed geological mapping In the preliminary stage of Investigation to demarcate significant geological and structural features of the area 4.1.2.2 Topographic sections shall be taken on I : I 000 scale at approximately 30 m interval covering the entire area noted In 4.1.2.1. The geology of the area shall be plotted along these sections and projected to the power house g-rade to develop forecast secnons for further geotechnical evaluation. 4.1.3 Subsurface Explorauon 4.1.3.1 Drifts - A mimmum of one drift for each alternanve shall be excavated normal to general trend of contours towards the power house
location to explore the extent of relief or slump JOInting and depth to sound rock, nature and spacing of prominent JOints, fractures and shear zones, at and around the power house cavity. This drift will also help in providing data on ground water condttrons. The drift shall preferably be 2'2 m x 1'5 m in sections and wherever possible it shall be located near the proposed haunch elevation of the power house cavity. A few cross cuts may also become necessary for exploration of specific features.

4.1.3.2 Diamond core dnllmg' - Selected drilling, wherever feasible, for one or 2 holes may be required to demarcate rock cover over the cavyit and Inhologrc conttnutty of the rock units harbouring the power house

cavity and to explore the existence of solution cavities, if any. Each hole shall be drilled down to the base of the proposed power house unit and water perrneabihty tests shall be performed in its entire length in stages which shall normally be restricted to 3 m [see IS : 5529 (Part 1)-1969* and IS: 5529 (Part II )-1973t]. Water bearing conditions shall also be observed in the entire section of the hole.

4.2 Prelimiaary Stage Investigatioas
4.2.1 Here the object of mvesugarions IS to select the most suitable site for a power house based on the interpretations of surface and subsurface exploration data, comparative and subsurface exploration data, and comparative evaluation of the vanous alternatives. Detailed geologIcal mapping shall be carrred out concurrently with the recommended subsurface explorations and at least the following features shall be recorded:
a) Surface geological mapping shall establish:

..;

I) Varrous hthological umts present m the area, their altitudes and continuity. susceptrbihty to weathering, geometry of the structural weak planes such as joints, nature of filling of the planes of drscontinuity, slip planes, shear zones, folds and faults;
ir) Demarcation of covered area WIth remarks on the nature of the material, creep and slide features; lll) Ground water conditions; iv) Existence and nature of spnngs - hot or cold; and v) Pressure of any oil or gas shows.

b) The observations in the exploratory tunnel should include: I) Lnhologic characters of the various rock units; II} Their amenabihty to tunnelling, 111) LImit of slump JOInts or glide cracks, iv) Depth to sound rock; vi Nature, spacing and contmuity of prominent joints, shp planes. minor and major shear zones; and VI) Study of stress field. c) Collection of core samples of various rock types for determination of elastic and engineermg properties m the laboratory.
"Oode of practice for tn-sdu permeability tests : Part I Tests In overburden. fCode of practice for UJ-SJtu permeabrhty test" Part II Tests In bedrock

12

IS , 10060 . 1981 4.2.2 Based on the results of subsurface exploranons, suitable recommendations regarding the location and onentation of the power house cavity shall be made. A programme of subsurface exploration by drift extending up to the tentative power house location shall be made in order to have a detailed assessment of the geological discontinuities present at the power house site. The dnft shall preferably run along the long axis of the power house having at least 3 cross cuts on either side of the power house axis and extending up to the power house walls. The drifts may preferably be kept at haunch level of the roof arch. If these studies indicate the presence of adverse geological discontinuities with reference to the long axis of the power house, the orientation of the cavity shall be suitably modified. In general, It IS undesirable to have prominent geological discontinuities parallel or nearly parallel to the long axis of the power house or along high walls and rock cuts. 4.3 Detailed and Pre-design Stage Investigations 4.3.1 The object of the invesugatron is to provide a fairly clear picture of the existing geological conditions hkely to be present at the power house cavity for deSign of the cavity and outhne 01 the excavation programme and treatment. 4.3.2 Critical geological observations shall be made m the exploratory tunnels made in the cavIty area and the drIll holes dnIJed earlier. Rock mechanics studies regarding geological discontmurties shall be correlated with surface observations and drill hole data. SUItable number of tests shall be performed for the deterrmnanon of in-sua modulus of elasticity, Poission's ratio and determination of stress field in vanous directions, (see IS; 7292-1974* and IS: 7317-l974t) and also the properties of important shear zone materials and joint fillings. 4.3.3 Investigations shall cover an area around the cavity of 3 to 5 times its larger dimension, depending upon the geological cornplexiues deciphered in the preliminary investigation stage 4.4 Construction Stage Investigations 4.4.1 The object of construction stage investigation IS to explore and systematically record in 3 dimensions the geological features and related problems met with which are not revealed durmg the pre-design stage explorations or were revealed durmg the pre-design stage and their explorations were deferred for the construction stage. Such explorations shall be done accordmg to the day-to-day requirements of the projects. A complete record of the foundation features shall be mamtamed at this stage This is essentral for the solution of post-construction problems, if any.

IS : 10060 - 1981 5. THERMAL POWER STATIONS
5.1 Investigations for thermal power houses shall generally be on the lines suggested for hydroelectric surface power houses ( see 3) and shall cover points appropriate to rhrs type [see also 2.3.2(c) ]. For general prmciples and procedures to be followed for investigation and sampling, reference may be made to IS : 1892-1979*.

6. NUCLEAR POWER HOUSES 6.1 Reconnaissance Stage 6.1.1 In this stage, thc most SUitable sites are reconnoitered from geological, engineering and environmental considerations. Prior to field VIsits it is preferable to study the area wrth the help of aenal photographs,m the scale of either I . 60 000 or I . 25 000, to mark out the lithological umts, geornophological features, hke old slide debns, and tectonic features mcludmg lmeament trends of the area. The last mentioned study shall be done with an objective of obtaining evidences for and against recent activity along faults. These studies shall also be directed towards geohydrol"8'Cal characterrsncs of the area. Linuted ground checks are called for aile.- a detailed photogeological assessment of the area. At this stage itself, to select alternatrve sites for further surveys and exploration, data on the seismic status of the area within a radius of 100 km of the sue shall be collected and analysed. Wherever study of existing I : 2 000000 tectonic maps indicate the existence of seismogcnie features, the area of photo coverage may be extended to a radius of 300 km. A mobile seismic instrumentation unit to record micro-earthquake may be requrred in case seismogenic features are suspected WIthin the area studied as above. 6.1.2 Topographic survey maps in I : 25 000 or I : 15000 scale shall be used as base maps for geological mapping during the reconnaissance stage. Spring levels and general ground water table conditions existing m the area shall also be assessed. 6.2 PrelilDinary Stage
6.2.1 Surveys -- The object of the invesuganon is to carry out detailed geological mapping m I I 000 scale WIth a view to portraying the features of the promising alternative sites. ThIS geological mapping shall aim to establish the followmg:
a) The varrous lithological units present m the area, their altitude and continuity with a view to establish bands of sufficient WIdth of hard and homogeneous materral SUItable for founding the heavy umts of the power house.
"Code of practtce for subsurface mvestigations fat foundations (first reViSum 1.

14

IS : 10060 - 1981
b) The validity of the faults interpreted from photogeologic studies, and if proved, their status of activity on field evidences shall be collected and plotted. In addition similar studies of faults, interpreted from field mapping which were not picked up by photogeological studies, shall also be carried out.

6.2.2 Subsurface Exploration - In areas covered by debris or terrace gravels, geophysical surveys can be considered for evaluating depth and nature of bedrock along With level of ground water table. A few diamond drill holes, preferably of NX or larger size, shall be drilled for establishing bedrock and for obtaining the cores for determimng physical properties like compressive strength and modulus of elasticity by laboratory tests both under dry and wet condiuons (after 72 hours of soaking in water). In such drill holes, the water table If encountered, shall be carefully, recorded and, m addiuon, cychc water percolation tests shall be performed for determining the permeabihty of the foundation rnaterral It IS essential that dnllmg be done for a depth of 10 m into fresh rock and dunng drillmg double core barrel unhsing bottom discharge bits shall be used. In case
of alluvial formations, wash borings, auger holes, penetration tests, etc,

shall be done to assess the nature of the sub-soil material and also to obtain undisturbed samples for the determination of soil properties.

6.2.2.1 In case of sandy alluvial foundation strata, geophysical blast test shall be done to determine whether the material IS liable to hquefy under seismic disturbances.

6.2.3 Geohydrological Surveys - Date-wise data on the occurrence of springs and water table m dug wells or tube wells of the area shall be collected. The repeat measurements of these shall be done before and after the monsoon season and water table maps prepared. Data on aquifer characterrstics shall be collected and depth to water table maps prepared. The chemical quality of the ground water shall also be determined.
Layout of the structure vtS-a-vlS the geology having been generally fixed, further exploration shall be carried out by cormg holes drilled at the corners and grade, for deterrrumng the nature of the actual foundation material and ItS physical characteristzcs, mcludmg m-situ perrneabihty. The site of the lighter structures shall also be investigated by a few drill holes or trial pits. In addition, in-SItu load bearing tests may be conducted m overburden, alluvial and soft rock foundation to evaluate precisely the deformation characteristics. From these data, detailed geological sections for use in the final design of the structure shall be prepared.

6.4 Con.traction Stage
6.4.1 Depending upon the design and engineering requirements of day-to-day work, explorations and recording of geological features and related problems, revealed during the pre-construction or construction stage shall be carried out to guide the treatment of weak zones encountered during excavation of the foundation. A complete record of the foundation features shall be maintained at tlus stage. This is essential for the solution ofthe post-construction problems, if any The foundation grade geotechnical maps shall be prepared in I : 100 scale, giving details of the majorjrnmor rock structures, lithological varrations, nature and abundance of the planes of discontinuities with their spatial distribution and nature of infilling material, if any, and water table condiuons.
